title: Trends and causes of maternal mortality in Taiyuan, China, 2016–2024: A population-based observational study
content:
by Fang Wang, Hailan Yang

Background

Although China has made major advances in maternal health, city-level epidemiological evidence on maternal mortality remains scarce. Using maternal surveillance data from Taiyuan (2016–2024), we assessed trends in the maternal mortality ratio (MMR), examined causes of death, and identified associated factors to inform region-specific strategies for reducing MMR.

Methods

We extracted and validated data on maternal deaths and live births from the Taiyuan Municipal Maternal and Child Health Annual Reports. MMR was calculated per 100,000 live births. Poisson regression was used to examine temporal trends, and chi-square or Fisher’s exact tests were used for between-group comparisons. Analyses were stratified by geographic region, cause of death, and place of death; the study period was divided into three phases (2016–2018, 2019–2021, 2022–2024) for subgroup analysis.

Results

Between 2016 and 2024, Taiyuan recorded 424,392 live births and 33 maternal deaths, yielding an overall MMR of 7.76 per 100,000 live births (95% CI 5.35 to 10.92). Urban MMR declined significantly (P < 0.0001), whereas rural MMR showed no significant temporal change (P = 0.313) and remained higher than urban levels (9.57 vs 7.58 per 100,000). Indirect obstetric causes accounted for 66.7% of maternal deaths, compared with 33.3% for direct causes, with no significant temporal trends in either category. Women aged 30–39 years accounted for 63.6% of maternal deaths, and 83.9% of deaths occurred in tertiary hospitals.

Conclusion

Taiyuan has maintained a low MMR through sustained investment in maternal healthcare; however, substantial urban-rural disparities remain. Indirect obstetric causes predominated among maternal deaths, suggesting a transition in the spectrum of maternal causes of death. Continued efforts to strengthen rural maternal health services and promote equitable, life-course-oriented maternal care are essential to further reduce preventable maternal deaths.
